title: Grateful Dead Live at Field House, U. of Cincinnati on 1970-04-03
lineage: SBD > ? >  bootleg CD > pitch correction and retracking > SHN

ai_review.summary: A strong 1970 soundboard capture featuring the debut of “Candyman,” stellar Pigpen moments and sweet Jerry vocals, with good‑to‑excellent audio despite occasional acoustic buzzing.
ai_review.review: These reviews rave about a historic 1970 show that includes the first performance of “Candyman” and standout renditions of Deep Elem Blues, Black Peter, Good Lovin' and Lovelight. Pigpen is described as “smokin’,” and Jerry’s singing is called unusually sweet throughout. The soundboard source is praised as solid for its era, with only minor buzzing in the acoustic set and a well‑balanced overall mix.

ai_rating.rationale: All eight reviewers give 4–5 stars, highlighting exceptional musical moments and consistently good recording quality; weighted average (70 % show, 30 % recording) yields a rating above 4½.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear and strong for the era; occasional buzzing on the acoustic set and minor pitch‑speed quirks noted, but overall balanced mix with correct pitch (China Cat Sunflower in G).

show_quality.setlist_flow: The set is praised for its rare first‑time songs (Candyman, FOD/FOTD) and a tight acoustic segment; transitions such as NFA into Lovelight are highlighted as especially smooth.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His vocals are described as unusually sweet on Deep Elem Blues, Candyman and Black Peter; overall guitar work praised.
band_member_comments.Phil: Consistently amazing bass playing and locked‑in interplay with Jerry throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir is noted for paying homage to Pigpen during Good Lovin' and Lovelight, but no specific comment on his instrumental performance.
